title: O’Reilly Gives $1 Million+ to 40 Charities
summary: O'Reilly Auto Parts distributes more than $1 Million from charity golf tournaments to Springfield, Missouri-area charities, setting a record.
body_markdown:
# O’Reilly Gives $1 Million+ to 40 Charities


by[Sonya Cox](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/author/scox35/)


| Nov 20, 2026


|[Content](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/category/content/) ,[Highlighted Story](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/category/highlighted-story/) ,[Top News](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/category/top-news/)


Just in time to meet additional holiday needs, O’Reilly Auto Parts has distributed more than $1 million dollars to 40 Springfield, Missouri – area charities, setting a record for both the gift total and the number of charities impacted.


While the[O’Reilly Automotive Foundation, Inc.](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/foundation/) awards grants across the United States, the proceeds from the company’s two annual charity golf tournaments stay in its hometown of Springfield, Missouri.


That tradition started in 1999 with one small tournament and a single charity. In 2017, The Community Foundation of the Ozarks began holding the fund and facilitating the grant application process. Since then, O’Reilly Charity Golf Classic tournaments have raised and distributed more than $6 million dollars.


“When we read through the grant applications, we see both the needs in our communities and the incredible way local organizations are stepping up to help,” said Julie Gray, O’Reilly vice president of Corporate Services. “We’re so happy to be part of the solution, and want the community to know that despite this record total, there are additional needs we were not able to fund. I’d ask those who can to consider supporting these nonprofits and others in our area.”


*Rosalie O’Reilly Wooten (center) joins O’Reilly team members Kari Hamra, Brianna Morgan, Julie Gray, Macy Ballard and Jaclyn Gallivan to celebrate the milestone of more than $1 million in charity golf tournament funds.*


On Wednesday, Nov. 18, O’Reilly Auto Parts handed out these grants:


- **The Arc of the Ozarks**
$25,000 for educational support programs at Rivendale Institute for Learning and Autism Services, and Infinity Academy, both of which offer education to children with special needs.
- **Big Brothers Big Sisters** $25,000 in operational funds to match volunteer adults with children for one-to-one mentoring programs.
- **Boys & Girls Clubs of Springfield** $25,000 in operational support to ensure it can continue to serve more than 6,000 children and teens each year with educational programs in a safe environment.
- **Breast Cancer Foundation of the Ozarks** $25,000 to support the organization’s non-medical financial help for patients going through active breast cancer treatment.
- **Care to Learn** $25,000 in operational funds to support its efforts to meet kids’ health, hunger and hygiene needs in more than 60 area school districts and communities.
- **Catholic Charities of Southern Missouri** $15,000 to help fund the Habits of Harvest cooking classes at LifeHouse Crisis Maternity Home.
- **The Child Advocacy Center** $25,000 to support the organization’s work to provide abused children a safe place to heal as they undergo a forensic interview and medical exam.
- **Children’s Smile Center** $25,000 in operational support to purchase more than 12,000 oral hygiene kits for community distribution.
- **Community Partnership of the Ozarks** $25,000 for operational support at the O’Reilly Center for Hope, which brings together 20 partner agencies that help low to moderate income families.
- **CASA – Court Appointed Special Advocates** $25,000 in operational funds to provide advocacy for children in foster care as they navigate the court system.
- **CoxHealth Foundation (new recipient)** $20,000 for the Bridge for Hope program, which provides patients with assistance for things like prescriptions, medical equipment, and transportation.
- **Crosslines Community Outreach** $50,000 for operational support and an emergency generator to protect its fresh and frozen food pantry items.
- **Developmental Center of the Ozarks** $25,000 in operational funding for its CONNECTS program, which helps individuals build independence through hands-on community experiences.
- **The Doula Foundation of Mid-America** $25,000 in operational funds for its Baby’s First Year initiative, which helps families in need create a safe, stable home environment.
- **The Drew Lewis Foundation** $25,000 for their Bikes & Brew Bodega coffee shop, and building improvements at the Fairbanks community center.
- **Eden Village (new recipient)** $25,000 to furnish 28 tiny homes with chairs and dining room sets for individuals who have experienced homelessness.
- **FosterAdopt Connect** $25,000 in operational support for Sammy’s Window and Sharehouse services, a clothing bank and food pantry that support foster children and their families.
- **Girl Scouts of the Missouri Heartland (new recipient)** $15,000 so more girls can participate in the Brave Minds. Kind Hearts. program, which helps build confidence, emotional resilience and healthy relationships.
- **Good Samaritan Boys Ranch** $25,000 to help furnish its Step Ahead facility, which helps teenage boys learn and practice the skills needed before they transition into independent living.
- **GYN Cancers Alliance** $20,000 for education, resources and support for local women and caregivers affected by gynecologic cancers, including non-medical financial assistance.
- **Harmony House** $48,000 in operational support for its domestic violence shelter, outreach case management services and prevention education programs, as well as funding for new air conditioning units.
- **In Time of Need Foundation** $15,000 to support its funeral and cremation program for families who cannot pay for a loved one’s funeral expenses.
- **I Pour Life** $17,000 for costs associated with client and data management software to support its positive youth development programs, which assist at-risk older youth, ages 16-24.
- **Isabel’s House** $25,000 in operational funds for the crisis nursery, which provides immediate refuge for children whose families are in crisis to prevent child abuse and neglect and strengthen families.
- **The Kitchen** $50,000 in operational funds to support the organization, including rental subsidies for residents of Franciscan Villa.
- **Kiwanis Club of Ozark Empire** $20,000 to provide more than 2,000 Springfield-area kids with high-quality new shoes.
- **Least of These** $50,000 to buy food for its Christian County food pantry, which serves more than 3,400 people each month.
- **Lost and Found Grief Center** $25,000 for operational funds to support its free grief support services, including special holiday programming, summer camps, and counseling support.
- **Lutheran Family and Children’s Services** $15,000 in funding support for its adoption and parenting services, including case management, supportive counseling and education.
- **The Betty and Bobby Allison Ozarks Counseling Center** $25,000 in operational funds for its work in providing low-cost mental health services to those in need.
- **Ozarks Food Harvest** $50,000 to buy 75,000 meals for families in need and to stock weekend backpacks for 79 children, so they can take nutritious meals home from school each Friday.
- **Ozarks Literacy Council** $25,000 to buy books to support tutoring and literacy development by ensuring children have access to high-quality, relevant and engaging books.
- **Ozarks Regional YMCA** $25,000 to support the Y Academy Summer Day Camp, which serves up to 300 kids each summer.
- **The Rebound Foundation** $25,000 to support transitional housing for women and children who are transitioning out of domestic violence shelters.
- **Rescue One (new recipient)** $10,000 for its efforts to care for animals and the people who love them, including its SafePet services, which coordinate temporary foster care for the pets of people leaving domestic violence situations.
- **Ronald McDonald House Tooth Truck** $20,000 for supplies needed to complete the dental treatment plans for approximately 940 children.
- **Springfield Community Gardens (new recipient)** $10,000 to help support 15 community gardens and two farms, which grow and distribute fresh produce to more than 7,000 local households.
- **Springfield Dream Center** $30,000 for two programs. Toddler Time offers learning and literacy activities, and The Village offers mothers mentorship.
- **The Victim Center** $30,000 for crisis response, advocacy and counseling for people who have survived a violent or sexual crime.
- **Victory Mission and Ministry** $40,000 for operational support for its shelters, recovery programs and workforce development programs.


“We strive to give back to all communities where we do business, but are truly humbled to always support our community here in Springfield where it all began with just one store in 1957,” Gray said. “On behalf of O’Reilly Auto Parts, I want to thank these organizations, all the suppliers and vendors who sponsor our tournaments, and the team members who make the events possible each year. None of this would be possible without them.”
